svg.text: THE SOCIAL STRUCTURE · NINE COMPOSITIONS · ONE CANON
Not assets, not environments — the shape of everyday life. Each diagram is a topology of encounters: where routines cross, friendships become accidents waiting to happen.
+ everyone crosses everyone, daily; the town has one unmistakable stage
− no gradient — the centre exhausts itself, the edges die; quiet is accidental, not
▸ public stories only: markets, announcements, spectacles — intimacy has nowhere to
one street carries the whole town
+ maximum repeated encounters — the same faces at the same times, every day
− no shortcuts, no discovery, no second route; the ends are exile; one blockage stops the
▸ routine stories: the commuter who nods, the timed hellos — warm but monotone
an orbit with the green at its centre
+ no dead ends; two directions mean chance meetings; the centre is always near
− all places equal → no heart, no climax; compression never happens; navigation is
▸ coincidence stories — but few anchored memories; nowhere is THE place
the ground across the water, one bridge
+ matchday becomes pilgrimage; the bridge funnels the whole town into one shared moment
− the ground is exiled on the thirteen quiet days; the river cuts more than it joins
▸ ritual stories: the crossing, the bridge meeting, the returning crowd at dusk
market at one end, Oak at the other
+ busy and quiet built in; walking has direction; District 01 is this structure
− two hearts can split loyalty; the connecting street must never fail or both centres do
▸ contrast stories: commerce vs. calm, the walk between moods
+ football permeates — literally; matchday is effortless
− violates the brief: the ground dominates and lies empty 13 days of 14; a dead heart
▸ football stories only — the town has no life to return to on Sunday
+ neighbourhood identity — each hamlet its own anchor; natural rivalries (street
− cross-town encounters are rare; friends happen within hamlets, strangers stay strangers
▸ belonging and rivalry stories: our end, their end, the derby inside the town
+ generations overlap by design — the school run crosses the shopping run twice
− the rhythm collapses in holidays; adults without children orbit outside it
▸ growing-up stories: the walk that shortens as you age, teachers met in the market
two lines of different frequency, crossing at the Oak
+ the daily line (school–bakery–market) crosses the weekly line
everyone, at different cadences; quiet edges survive
− the crossing must be sized with care — too small congests, too large dissipates
▸ every kind: routine on the daily line, ritual on the weekly, and their collisions at
AGAINST THE NINE QUESTIONS (condensed to five)
DISTRICT 01 IS THE WEAVE’S CROSSING, ZOOMED IN

CANONICAL — T9 THE WEAVE: a daily line (school · bakery · market) and a weekly line (homes · Oak · bridge · ground) crossing at ONE point — the Oak, the pub on its corner, quiet lanes ringing the edges.
The ground sits across the water at the weekly line’s end — floodlights and sound, never dominance — and on matchday the bridge turns the whole town into one procession (T4’s gift).

WHY IT SUPPORTS THE SIMULATION — encounters are made by routines of DIFFERENT FREQUENCY sharing one node: daily crosses weekly crosses seasonal at the Oak, so familiar strangers are manufactured by geometry (Recognition, CD-003),

friendships become accidents of repetition (CD-001), quiet edges give dyads somewhere to become stories, and the school tide guarantees the generations collide twice a day. Deterministic tides make watchable crowds (CD-006).
REJECTED FOR THE RECORD — T6 (stadium at the heart) fails the brief outright: a dead centre 13 days of 14. T3 (the ring) has no heart at all. Both kept on the board so they are never re-argued.
